turns.q:
Your response was: "Looked at it. Checkout flow. Nearly missed the submit button. It barely registered visually — took a moment to find the action I needed."

We want to understand what you meant by "nearly missed the submit button", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The “Place Order” button sits below the more prominent “Continue Shopping” button, so the primary checkout action appears lower in the hierarchy.

B) The “Place Order” button is positioned near the bottom of the layout, beneath the payment details and secondary action, making it feel buried.

C) The “Place Order” button appears visually muted compared with surrounding elements, so it does not stand out as the main action in the wireframe.

D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
What specifically makes the “Place Order” button look muted here — its size, contrast, position under “Continue Shopping,” or something else in the layout?
turns.a: Lighter one disappeared into the background. Almost looked inactive.

turns.q: If someone saw the light “Place Order” button exactly as shown, would they read it as the checkout action being available, or as something unavailable until more information is provided?
turns.a: Eye went straight to 'Continue Shopping' — that one registered. Had to scan for 'Place Order.' When I found it, wasn't sure it was the right one. Re-read the label to confirm. Took longer than it should have.

turns.q: When the light “Place Order” area disappears into the background like that, what does it suggest the lower action area of this checkout layout is getting wrong structurally?
turns.a: Solid high-contrast fill on 'Place Order' — a real color, not gray. WCAG AA minimum: 4.5:1 contrast ratio for the label text. Label up to at least 14–16px. Gray on gray at 12px reads as disabled — it fails WCAG AA and it fails as a primary CTA. Fix: brand color fill, white label text, readable size. One button. That's it.
